writeup: TIC 447456051 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.0777 days. Data from TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 1.60%, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 77.3 using the Box Least Squares method. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis provides additional support, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 8.4, though the centroid offset of 4.5 arcsec from the target's position warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.60 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine target. This candidate passed all data quality checks.
